mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 900K signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 7% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which tends to precede negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 0.5% combined with a concurrent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals a deflationary monetary regime, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower borrowing costs and stimulus effects.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL < 100 (i.e., <1%) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in retail sales (RSAFS) above the previous quarter's average by more than 3% signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND RSAFS > previous quarter average + 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate of more than 0.2 percentage points for three consecutive months, despite rising payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals structural labor market imbalances that precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > +0.2% for three consecutive months AND PAYEMS monthly change > 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing activity, which tends to precede positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
